174.t: Felix Goff, Eugene Porter and other saxophonists in his band
174.s: He names clarinet and sax players from his Desvigne and Ridgley days, including Felix Goff and tenor man Eugene Porter from Jackson, Mississippi.
174.q: What did he play? We played, we played tenor saxophone. And, we had to coach him to get up to take a course after he got the fright off him. He was tough, I'm telling you. And then he had McLaren, no time, no time, no time, I said a couple of months. He was sitting in the back of that plan and…

175.s: Brief talk about Handy, an alto saxophonist and clarinetist who played gut-bucket style.
175.q: Right. And if you was the type of musician you couldn't play a gut bucket style, you were just lost. And there was another guy down there who was a tremendous musician. I also found out that he wasn't much of a reader either and this was this, what was his name, Handy? Oh John Handy.

183.t: Reel 2 begins with Alfred on saxophone players in his California band
183.s: On a new reel, Allen asks Alfred about saxophonists such as Red Spikes who played in his California band.
183.q: Let's see, this is Bob Watts' Reel 2. It's May the, I keep saying May, February 28th, 1963. Since you're here, this is Alfred Williams, I wanted to ask you, you say you had some saxophone players with Orion in California when you were out there? Yeah, Red Spikes played, you see, Red played Tether.…

773.s: Discussion of saxophonist Henry Julian, who lost his mind, and his relative Frank Crump.
773.ch: Arnold DePass's life and the Cadillac years
773.q: Well, he, let's see, he was about his age to be now. I mean, well, he would maybe be about in his fifties now. In his early fifties, you know. He would be about Henry Julian, you know. And he was, oh, great musician, you know. But he lost his mind. And he had, that was some of his relation, this…

839.t: Reese Colbert and the DuConge family
839.s: Brief talk of saxophonist Colbert and the DuConges, with Pete married to Bricktop.
839.q: They all come from down there. He's Pete de Conje and all them. Albert de Conje, all the on there.

151.t: Saxophonist Al Wilson and Cormick Scott
151.s: Reason confirms Al Wilson played with Nellie Lutcher and names another player from Texas.
151.q: Yeah, I know Al Wilson. Oh, yeah. Yeah. He played all that. In fact, Al Wilson was with us with Nellie Latchett.

799.t: Leadership of the Owls and Dan LeBlanc's sax sessions
799.s: Frank Netto led the Owls; Eddie Miller took clarinet solos; Dan LeBlanc wrote for afternoon sax get-togethers.
799.q: At that time Frank Netto when I played with him. Pinky had left them and Crum had left them and a lot of, most of the original band had left except Frank and Dan LeBlanc and Frank Netto were the two original, two of the members from the original band.

121.s: How the sax player nicknamed Nose settled in New Orleans, was a nice man, and later repaired saxophones.
121.ch: The Dew Drop, Blue Eagle and visiting stars
121.q: Yeah. No, no, not necessarily no problems. I mean, he was doing drugs? Uh-uh. Okay. That's why I always thought it was Nose, because he did drugs. No, uh-uh, no. The cocaine? No, he had a big nose, but it was other things.

776.t: Eugene Sedric on the boat with Fate Marable
776.s: Eugene Sedric played with Marable and is still going strong in New York.
776.q: Yeah, Gene Cedric. Little Fat Follower. That's him.

643.t: Musicians from the neighborhood: Hall Boys, Herb Tree, Marshall
643.s: He names musicians from the area, including the Hall Boys, Kid Ory, and George Tree's son Herb, a saxophonist in California who played with Marshall.
643.q: Yeah, and the Hall Boys, they came from here. Ken Ory, you come from here? Yeah Ken Ory, he's from the- Yeah, they're over in, uh, the other family. This is Austin, he was- He was from the area too, but he was in a home. And, uh, that's the, uh, I call, uh, The Hall Boys, you got them Hall Boys,…

835.s: Humphrey met Klemmer in Don Ellis's band and describes him as an early New Age saxophonist who disappeared from public view.
835.q: Well I see that John was maybe one of the first New Age saxophone players, you know, with what he was doing back, way back when. A phenomenal player. Really a wonderful jazz player. But I think John had some, maybe some psychological problems and so it kind of made him disappear from the public for…

840.s: They wonder what became of Klemmer. Magnusson relays news from Oscar Castro-Neves and calls him the Kenny G before Kenny G.
840.q: You know I saw Oscar Castro-Neves just Friday night, because we hadn’t seen each other in quite a while and we worked together on that, and I was asking him, because I heard a new record on the radio of Oscar and John together. This was just like six months ago. So I asked Oscar I says, “Did you…
